judgments.reasoning_cat1: A block-capital notice stating claims must be 'FIRST MADE ... AND REPORTED ... DURING THE POLICY PERIOD' with no mention of the extended reporting period; the flat statement is capable of being read as an operative condition or as a mere caption.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared perfectly with Insuring Agreement I.A./I.B. and Section VIII, which allow a claim to be reported during an 'extended reporting period' after the policy period ends.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short integration statement listing the documents constituting the policy; nothing in it carries two meanings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the endorsement list and with IX.K (Changes and Assignment), which likewise requires changes to be by attached endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical is garbled ('litem, 3.a.', stray commas) and '100 % minimum-earned' is a percentage stated in a slot elsewhere called a 'premium percentage', leaving what is earned on day one arguably uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits awkwardly against IX.A.3, which contemplates 'remaining unearned premium' earned pro rata and a pro rata refund within thirty days — impossible if 100% is minimum-earned at inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same block-capital notice as the Declarations version; the unqualified 'reported ... during the policy period' overstates the reporting condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in emphasis with I.A./I.B. and Section VIII.B., which deem claims reported in an extended reporting period to have been reported on the last day of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple signpost that quoted terms are defined in Section V.; no term in it is ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements add defined terms outside Section V. (e.g. 'business interruption loss', 'product pollution'), a minor mismatch with the statement that definitions live in Section V.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/reliance recital; 'in reliance upon all statements made in the Application' is boilerplate rather than genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with IX.F. Representations and the Fraud or Misrepresentation exclusion; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A lead-in conditioning coverage on the Coverages being 'identified on the Declarations'; plain and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplemental coverages are added by endorsement rather than 'identified on the Declarations', a small tension with II.G. which expressly contemplates Supplemental Coverages.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'first commence, in their entirety, during the policy period' is a genuinely contestable phrase for a continuing or creeping pollution condition, as is 'arising out of'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This same subsection is deleted and replaced in its entirety twice — by Endorsement 5.II (retroactive-date version) and again by Endorsement 10.I (transportation version) — leaving two competing replacements of one clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'commenced, in whole or part, prior to the policy period' is workable but its boundary against Coverage A's 'in their entirety during' is arguable for conditions straddling inception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with I.A. and with Endorsement 5's retroactive-date rewrite of Coverage A, the allocation of a straddling condition between Coverages A and B is not fully resolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'satisfactory evidence' and 'the same, continuous, repeated, or related pollution condition' are elastic phrases that decide how many retentions apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the SIR definition (V.AA.) and III.D., though the Catastrophe Management endorsement adds a separate $100,000 retention without expressly reconciling with this one-retention rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A per-condition limit cross-referring to Item 2.b.; the only soft term, 'related pollution condition', is defined by usage throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I expressly deletes and replaces this subsection, so the base text is superseded rather than contradicted, but a reader must notice the replacement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain aggregate-limit statement keyed to Item 2.c.; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 2.c. is $9,000,000 while Item 4.'s Total Policy Aggregate is $7,000,000, so the 'maximum liability' language must be subordinated to II.G. to make sense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mirror of the Coverage A per-condition limit; mechanical and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Superseded by Endorsement 6.I.E., which adds an undefined 'covered operations' qualifier absent here — a divergence between the two versions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Plain aggregate limit keyed to Item 3.c.; no contestable term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.I.F. replaces it and adds 'resulting from covered operations', an undefined limitation, so the two texts do not say the same thing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'subject to Subsections C., D., E. and F.' formula is circular with those subsections, which are themselves made subject to G.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Item 4. figure ($7,000,000) is smaller than the Coverage A aggregate in Item 2.c. ($9,000,000), so the Declarations and this clause cannot both operate at face value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'continuous, repeated, or related' and the deeming of later-reported conditions into 'this policy period' are contestable, and 'no other policy shall respond' purports to bind instruments not before the reader.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations identify this as a renewal of an earlier policy, so the deeming rule interacts with prior-period coverage and with the Known Conditions exclusion in ways not spelled out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Duty to defend 'a claim to which this insurance applies' is standard, though the trigger for the duty ending on exhaustion or tender is stated compactly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.A. deletes and replaces this subsection with a differently worded exhaustion trigger keyed to the defense sublimit, so the base text no longer operates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Selection of legal counsel by the Insurer shall not be done without the consent of the insured' sits oddly with the Insurer's asserted 'right to select', and 'entitled by law to select independent counsel' imports an external standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in tension with Endorsement 6.IV.F., which gives the first named insured the right to select counsel after the defense sublimit is exhausted, and with IX.M. on unreasonable withholding of consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Casting retention of a consultant as both a 'right and the duty' of the insured, subject to the Insurer's prior written consent, is internally awkward but its operation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4.III.C. deletes and replaces this subsection in its entirety, and VII.C. (also replaced) states the consent rule again in slightly different words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence erosion rule; nothing to construe on its own wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.II.D. replaces it with a dedicated defense sublimit erosion rule, so the base sentence and the endorsement state different erosion mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not impose any additional unreasonable burdens on the insured' is a vague condition on the hammer clause and could be fought over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6.IV.F. restates a garbled version of the same hammer clause for post-exhaustion claims, creating two overlapping formulations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'located ... within the United States of America' is definite; the only stretch is applying 'located' to a migrating condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the covered-location schedules and with Endorsement 8's US-only non-owned disposal site definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition by cross-reference to endorsement; 'only those rights that are specified by endorsement' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 2 supplies the endorsement contemplated and limits Hoffman Rettig to vicarious liability, matching this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated definition; 'prospective medical monitoring costs' is a slightly unusual inclusion but its scope is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Employers Liability exclusion and the 'claim' definition without evident friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the hygienist to be 'mutually agreed upon', which could deadlock, but the qualification criteria are spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 excludes all fungi and legionella claims and costs, which leaves this fungi-specific definition (and its role in 'remediation costs') with nothing to operate on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'written assertion of a legal right' plus 'including, but not limited to, a government action' is a general-plus-specific formulation whose reach (e.g. regulatory letters, agency directives) is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This definition is deleted and replaced twice, by Endorsement 8.II and again by Endorsement 11.II, each 'solely with respect to' its own coverage, leaving the operative text layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and closed definition tied to carriers for hire; little room for two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 10.II deletes Subsection E. and substitutes 'transportation', yet the Vehicles exclusion in the base policy still carves back for 'contingent transportation', a term that no longer exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbering is corrupted (no '1.') and paragraph 2 refers to an Automatic Acquisition Endorsement that is not attached, though the 'if any' saves it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subsection F. is deleted and replaced in its entirety by both Endorsement 8.I and Endorsement 11.I with materially different texts, so which 'covered location' definition governs is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'imminent and substantial threat' is a standard but evaluative phrase, and the 72-hour window is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The emergency-response carve-out recurs in III.C., VII.C. and VI.H. consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defined by reference to a 'Schedule of Insured Contracts Endorsement', with 'if any' making the definition potentially empty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No such schedule is attached, so the Contractual Liability exclusion's carve-back for 'environmental indemnity obligations' has nothing to bite on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping list ending in 'guidance document' and 'risk-based corrective action guidance' — whether non-binding agency guidance or an emergency animal-health directive is 'environmental law' is a real question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives 'remediation costs' ('to the extent required by environmental law') and 'government action', so its breadth controls the size of the coverage grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition that does not itself state the length; 'during or subsequent to the end of the policy period' is loose but the operative periods are in Section VIII.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section VIII.A. limits entitlement to cancellation or nonrenewal, saying nothing about ordinary expiry, which this open definition does not resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but definite allocation of agency and payment duties; 'sole agent on behalf of all insureds' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits V.S. ('named insured' has the same rights except those reserved here) and IX.A.; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Self-referential ('byproducts produced or released by fungi' within the definition of fungi) but the intended breadth is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 deletes fungi from 'pollution condition' and excludes fungi claims outright, leaving this definition and the hygienist machinery orphaned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Depends entirely on 'acting pursuant to the authority of environmental law', which inherits whatever vagueness that term carries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with V.I. and V.D., a directive from an agricultural rather than environmental agency may or may not qualify, which matters for the whole coverage grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of pollutants followed by open categories ('waste materials, including ... medical, infectious and pathological wastes'), a classic ejusdem generis setup.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the 'pollution condition' definition, which Endorsement 12 rewrites while keeping 'illicit abandonment' intact, so this list survives the CAFO amendment unchanged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is circular — 'employee of ... any insured' — and 'while acting within the scope of his or her duties' may or may not qualify all the listed persons.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 'insured' sweeps in employees, the Insured vs. Insured exclusion and the Separation of Insureds condition (which speaks only of 'named insureds') do not mesh cleanly with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable legal costs' is evaluative but conventional; the category is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with III.D. and Endorsement 6's dedicated defense sublimit without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'waste with greater than specified quantities' does not say by whom specified, a small but real gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used only inside the 'pollution condition' and 'illicit abandonment' definitions and does not clash with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pinned to two named federal statutes; about as definite as a definition gets.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in W.3 and N.; no friction with other provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear cross-reference carve-out for rights reserved to the first named insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with V.K., II.A. (retention payment by 'another named insured') and IX.G.; no inconsistency found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long but statute-modelled definition; 'other such resources' is a catch-all after a list, a mild ejusdem generis point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is capped by Endorsement 12.III's $500,000 natural resource damage sublimit and folded into 'property damage'; the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and broad ('any disposal site or recycling facility not owned or operated by an insured'), with no temporal or permitting qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 8.II.U. deletes and replaces it with a far narrower, condition-laden definition, so the base text is displaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Paragraph 2. is syntactically broken — 'the period of time following the closing date ... or, as applicable, through the applicable expiration date' — and its start point is not stated coherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to an Automatic Acquisition Endorsement that is not attached, and paragraph 3 ('any shorter period resulting from cancellation') interacts with IX.A.2's statement that the cancellation date becomes the end of the policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The core coverage trigger: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant, contaminant, or pollutant, including smoke, soot, vapors ...' is the paradigm general-versus-specific list, and whether a biological agent is a 'contaminant' is exactly the kind of fight this wording invites.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 12 deletes this subsection in its entirety and substitutes a version without the fungi prong and excluding odor, so the base definition is displaced while other clauses (V.C., V.Y.) still assume the fungi prong exists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated heads, including 'diminished value of tangible property owned by a third-party'; definite as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Head 4 imports 'natural resource damages' which Endorsement 12 sublimits to $500,000, and the First-Party Property Damage exclusion removes the insured's own property; these fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reasonable expenses ... to the extent required by environmental law' is the pivotal limiter and is genuinely contestable, as is the fungi-specific fallback.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on 'environmental law' (V.I.) and on the fungi machinery that Endorsement 12 excludes, and the Insured's Internal Expenses exclusion cuts across the same costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any employee ... responsible for environmental affairs, control, or compliance' has an uncertain boundary in a large multi-site business.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It drives the Known Conditions, Intentional Non-Compliance and UST exclusions, so its breadth has consequences, but no clause contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straight cross-reference to Items 2.d. and 3.d.; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 4 adds a separate Catastrophe Management-specific retention without amending this definition, a small layering point the 'as otherwise designated by endorsement' language largely cures.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard terrorism definition with evaluative limbs ('appears that the intent is'), but heavily structured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds only the War or Terrorism exclusion and fits it; the Trade Sanctions endorsement is separate.
